question: Should OpenClaw expose Discord bot presence mutation to plugins as a public runtime API, and what gate, account scoping, audit behavior, and precedence model should it use?
rationale: The source already has internal presence mutation paths, but promoting one to `api.runtime.channel.discord` changes the public plugin contract and exposes a bot-token-backed mutation boundary to plugin code.

options.title: Approve a gated runtime API
options.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence` runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

options.title: Keep presence as message action only
options.body: Keep dynamic presence limited to the existing default-off `setPresence` message action and document that plugins should not mutate Discord presence directly.

options.title: Fold into self-profile direction
options.body: Defer this presence-only API behind the broader Discord self-profile decision if maintainers want one identity/profile contract instead of a separate runtime method.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated runtime API
recommendation.body: Add a narrow Discord-owned `updatePresence` runtime seam with explicit gating, account selection, docs, tests, and precedence rules.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on whether to reintroduce a plugin-specific runtime seam after the plugin-runtime boundary refactor.
